'''Thermal Spread''' is a ship [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effect]] that adds thermal conduits and radiator improvements to a [[Power Plant]], [[Frame Shift Drive]], or set of [[Thrusters]]. Its purpose is to reduce heat generation, but the modified attribute depends on the receiving module.<ref name="wiki">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Thermal_Spread Elite Dangerous Wiki: Thermal Spread], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

== Effects ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Module
! Modifier
! Additional effect
|-
| Power Plant
| Heat efficiency -10%
| None
|-
| Frame Shift Drive
| Thermal load -10%
| None
|-
| Thrusters
| Thermal load -10%
| Mass +5%
|}

A lower Power Plant heat-efficiency value is beneficial: it reduces the heat produced as the plant supplies power to the ship. The effect can therefore improve the thermal behaviour of many active modules at once.

On a Frame Shift Drive or Thrusters, Thermal Spread reduces the thermal load generated by that module. It does not directly change FSD range or boot time, thruster speed or handling, module power draw, or integrity. Thrusters also become 5% heavier.<ref name="inara-fsd">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/2/ INARA: Frame Shift Drive — Increased range], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref><ref name="inara-thrusters">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/6/ INARA: Thrusters — Clean], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

== Materials ==

The recipe depends on the module family:

{| class="wikitable"
! Module
! Required materials
|-
| Power Plant
| 5 Grid Resistors; 3 Vanadium; 1 Heat Vanes
|-
| Frame Shift Drive
| 5 Atypical Disrupted Wake Echoes; 3 Galvanising Alloys; 1 Heat Vanes
|-
| Thrusters
| 5 Iron; 3 Hybrid Capacitors; 1 Heat Vanes
|}

The Power Plant values are recorded by INARA's current Blueprint data.<ref name="inara-plant">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/13/ INARA: Power Plant — Overcharged], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref> Experimental Effects are installed once rather than progressed through Grades 1–5. The appropriate [[Engineers|Engineer]] must support the module family and be visited in person; [[Remote Engineering]] cannot add or replace an Experimental Effect.

== Power Plant use ==

Thermal Spread on a Power Plant affects the ship's underlying heat efficiency and is the broadest application of the effect. It is useful when:

* an Overcharged Power Plant supplies the required output but leaves the ship running hot;
* a low-emissions or stealth-oriented build prioritises a lower thermal signature;
* frequent fuel scooping, Frame Shift Drive charging, weapons fire, or Shield Cell Bank use pushes the heat budget;
* the ship has enough power and does not need the output increase from Monstered.

The 10% modifier applies to the Power Plant's current efficiency value. It is not a flat subtraction of ten percentage points from the ship's heat level.

== Frame Shift Drive use ==

Thermal Spread lowers heat generated by the FSD while it operates. It can help ships that approach their thermal limit during repeated jumps, close fuel-scooping passes, or charging near hot stars.

The effect competes with [[Mass Manager]] and Deep Charge, which directly improve jump performance. A ship that already handles heat comfortably will usually gain more travel value from a range effect; a heat-sensitive build may prefer Thermal Spread for safer charging.

== Thruster use ==

Thermal Spread reduces thruster thermal load but adds 5% to the module's mass. It can support cold-running or sustained-boost builds, particularly when thruster heat is a measured constraint.

The mass penalty and the loss of a competing Experimental Effect must both be considered. Drag Drives or Drive Distributors usually provide a more direct movement benefit, while [[Stripped Down]] reduces thruster mass. Use Thermal Spread only when thermal measurements show that it solves the build's actual limit.

== Practical limits ==

Thermal Spread reduces heat generation; it does not make a ship immune to overheating. Heat can still accumulate from weapons, Shield Cell Banks, Guardian or experimental modules, environmental sources, high power demand, and closed radiators during Silent Running.

Check the complete build in an outfitting planner and confirm it in flight. The cockpit heat percentage reflects the combined ship, not only the modified module.
